ticket_symptom: After re-indexing a repo, two symbols that share the same name — a class and a function called the same thing in one file, a helper defined inside two different functions, or two same-named defs in the same scope — sometimes end up pointing at the same entry / one overwrites the other. What gives each symbol its stable unique id across re-indexes, and how are same-name symbols kept from clashing?
entry_points: sutra/core/extractor/moniker.py:106 — MonikerBuilder._build returns f"{SCHEME} {self.language} {self.repo_name} {file_path} {descriptor}" (the 5-field space-delimited moniker)

sutra/core/extractor/adapters/python.py:471 — _disambiguate inserts (N) before the trailing suffix for the Nth genuine same-scope same-name collision
sutra/core/indexer.py:64 — _dedup_keep_first keep-first backstop that drops any symbols whose moniker still collides
mechanism: A symbol's stable id ("moniker") is built by MonikerBuilder._build (moniker.py:106) as a single space-delimited 5-field string: "sutra <language> <repo_name> <file_path> <descriptor>". Same-name symbols are disambiguated by three composed layers, not one: (1) file_path is a moniker field, so identical names in different files never collide; (2) the descriptor carries a kind suffix — ().  for function/method, # for class, .  for variable, /  for module (appended by the for_* methods) — plus a scope-chain PREFIX rendered by _prefix from an `enclosing` tuple, so a class and a function of the same name, or a nested/function-local helper vs a top-level def, get distinct descriptors; the python adapter's _scope_chain (python.py:142) computes that chain and deliberately does not stop at function boundaries so function-local symbols are self-describing. (3) For the rare genuine same-scope, same-name case (true "overloads"), _disambiguate (python.py:471) keeps the first occurrence's moniker and rewrites the Nth as `(N)` inserted before the terminating suffix; a final keep-first dedup backstop in indexer.py (_dedup_keep_first, line 64) drops any duplicate-moniker symbols that still slip through.
must_contain: The moniker is a space-delimited 5-field string `sutra <language> <repo_name> <file_path> <descriptor>` constructed by MonikerBuilder._build in sutra/core/extractor/moniker.py — file_path being one of those fields is what keeps same-named symbols in different files distinct.

The descriptor disambiguates by kind via an atomic trailing suffix — `().` for function/method, `#` for class, `.` for variable, `/` for module — and by a scope-chain prefix (rendered by _prefix from the `enclosing` chain, built by _scope_chain in python.py) so nested/function-local and top-level same-name symbols differ.

Genuinely same-scope same-name collisions are broken by _disambiguate in sutra/core/extractor/adapters/python.py, which keeps the first occurrence and inserts `(N)` before the trailing suffix for the Nth duplicate (with _dedup_keep_first in indexer.py as a final keep-first backstop).
ambiguity_risk: Low-to-moderate, and it is a completeness spread rather than two mutually-exclusive answers. The 'how the id is built' core is unambiguously moniker.py (MonikerBuilder._build), but the disambiguation logic is split across files: the kind-suffix + scope-prefix scheme lives in moniker.py (_prefix / for_* methods), the scope-chain that feeds it is _scope_chain in python.py, the true same-name tie-break is _disambiguate in python.py, and the final drop is _dedup_keep_first in indexer.py. A responder could stop at the suffix scheme and miss _disambiguate, or cite only _disambiguate and miss the file_path/suffix layers — but all live in the same sutra/core/extractor pipeline and none is a competing 'wrong-but-plausible' file, so the ticket is not drop-worthy.

ticket_symptom: When a query matches something by exact name, by keyword, and by vector similarity at the same time, the final ordering of search results looks off — one channel's single top hit floats to the top even when the other two channels agree on a different, better match further down. It then calls rrf_fuse() (fusion.py:12) which merges the lists by Reciprocal Rank Fusion: for each channel it re-assigns ranks itself via enumerate(results, start=1) (fusion.py:38) and adds 1.0/(k+rank) to each moniker's running score (fusion.py:39-40) with k=DEFAULT_RRF_K=60 (fusion.py:9). Raw per-channel scores (e.g. BM25 ~11.2 vs cosine ~0.83) are deliberately never compared — only ordinal ranks enter the sum, and the large k dampens the head so one channel's #1 cannot dominate consistent mid-rank agreement from the others. Results are then ordered by (-fused_score, moniker) for a deterministic tie-break (fusion.py:46), and each fused result carries the union of channel provenance plus {\"rrf\": score}.

The fused score of a document is the sum over channels of 1/(k + rank) with k = DEFAULT_RRF_K = 60, and the rank is assigned by fusion itself via enumerate(results, start=1) (fusion.py:38) — not read from the channel's own score

Raw channel scores are never compared across channels; only ordinal ranks enter the formula, and results are finally sorted by descending fused score with moniker as a deterministic tie-break (fusion.py:46)

Two nearby stages could be confused with the answer but are distinct: (a) the reranker (sutra/core/retrieval/reranker.py, invoked at pipeline.py:101-117) is an OPTIONAL cross-encoder pass that re-scores already-fused results, not the combining of the three channel lists; (b) GraphExpander.expand (expander.py) adds one-hop graph neighbors after fusion. sutra/core/resolver/heuristic.py:154-155 — HeuristicResolver.resolve: `candidates = by_name.get(name); if not candidates: continue` leaves an edge unresolved when no in-repo symbol bears the callee name
mechanism: The Python extractor never resolves calls at extraction time: for every call site it emits a Relationship(kind=CALLS, is_resolved=False, target_id=None, target_name=<literal callee name>) (python.py:667-674, and the method/class variants at 636-644/615-622). Phase-2's HeuristicResolver then tries to flip each unresolved CALLS to a known moniker by matching the callee short-name against in-repo symbol names; a callee that names a builtin or a third-party/library function (or any symbol not indexed) has no entry in the by_name pool, so resolve() hits `if not candidates: continue` (heuristic.py:154-155) and the edge stays is_resolved=False with target_id=None — such callees are explicitly excluded from the `matchable` denominator (resolver/base.py:14-19). Finally SqlGraphWriter._write_relationships iterates the relationships and executes `if not rel.is_resolved or rel.target_id is None: skipped += 1; continue` (sql_writer.py:355), so the dangling edge is NEVER inserted into the sutra_relationships table; only a `Skipped N unresolved relationships` line is printed to stderr (sql_writer.py:238-243). The queryable SQL graph therefore carries only resolved, in-repo CALLS edges, which is why callers/callees traversal omits library calls.
must_contain: The extractor emits every CALLS relationship as unresolved: is_resolved=False and target_id=None, keeping only the literal callee name in target_name — no in-repo resolution happens at extraction time (python.py extract, ~line 667-674).

A callee that is not an in-repo symbol (a builtin or third-party/library function) can never be resolved: the heuristic resolver finds no candidate for that name and leaves the edge is_resolved=False (it is excluded from ResolutionStats.matchable).

SqlGraphWriter._write_relationships (sql_writer.py:355) skips any relationship where `not rel.is_resolved or rel.target_id is None`, so unresolved/dangling edges are never written to the sutra_relationships table — only a skipped count is logged to stderr.
ambiguity_risk: Real, and it must be managed by ticket framing. 'How Sutra stores an unresolved call' has TWO divergent code paths: (1) the SQL/graph store — sql_writer.py:355 DROPS unresolved edges entirely (they never reach sutra_relationships); and (2) the JSON artifact — json_graph_exporter._relationship_to_dict (json_graph_exporter.py:228-233) PRESERVES the unresolved edge in graph.json with is_resolved=False, target_id=null, target_name kept. So a naive 'where is the unresolved edge stored' could correctly land on either. The ticket is deliberately phrased around the *queryable graph / callers-callees traversal* (which reads the SQL store and, in traversal.py:77 / expander.py:48, additionally skips any rel lacking target_id), pinning the intended answer to the sql_writer drop rather than the graph.json exporter. A grader must accept the SQL-store-drop mechanism and should not treat the graph.json-preserves-it path as the answer. Secondary minor ambiguity: the drop is enforced in three sibling spots (sql_writer.py:355, traversal.py:77, expander.py:48) — sql_writer is the canonical storage-side one.
